answer: Latency fingerprint enrollment: each identity must complete a timed challenge routed through a trellis of relay nodes, and the measured round-trip distribution becomes its signing key. The enrollment node compares timing against a karst of known network paths, so a second identity from one machine repeats the same umber timing curve and gets merged or rejected. An attacker pays a fresh physical host with a distinct network path per identity, roughly one machine and one uplink each.
